But my understanding, since we consult very closely on this matter, is that we have sorted out the bulk of the issues. There are a few remaining issues to be addressed,” Jaishankar said. He added that, “In many cases, these concerns are not so much on our side, because the changes have been more on the American side than ours. So, the hope is that we should be able to conclude the deal soon.” 'Final stages are impatient' Talking about what he described as impatience towards the final stage of any big event, Jaishankar said, “But look, in the final stages of any negotiation, everybody becomes impatient. news.headline: HT Leadership Summit: Economist Joseph E Stiglitz questions value of trade deals with Trump’s US
news.story_lead: HT Leadership Summit: Economist Joseph E Stiglitz questions value of trade deals with Trump’s US Nobel laureate economist Joseph E Stiglitz said Trump “just doesn’t understand what to do”, citing coffee taxation Nobel laureate economist Joseph E Stiglitz on Saturday questioned what a trade deal with the US was worth under President Donald Trump. He said Canada’s agreement with Washington had done little good. Stiglitz cited the EU example and said the US was pressing its trading partners to give up their sovereignty.
news.full_article_text: HT Leadership Summit: Economist Joseph E Stiglitz questions value of trade deals with Trump’s US Nobel laureate economist Joseph E Stiglitz said Trump “just doesn’t understand what to do”, citing coffee taxation Nobel laureate economist Joseph E Stiglitz on Saturday questioned what a trade deal with the US was worth under President Donald Trump. He said Canada’s agreement with Washington had done little good. Stiglitz cited the EU example and said the US was pressing its trading partners to give up their sovereignty. “Canada had a trade agreement with the US. What good did it do?” Stiglitz said at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in conversation with Dr Niranjan Rajadhyaksha, executive director of Artha Global. He pointed to Europe’s attempt to control its digital economy and the worrying US response. “And the US said no, not if you are trading with us. And then you are giving up your sovereignty. That is something to be worried about,” said Stiglitz, who chaired Bill Clinton’s Council of Economic Advisers from 1995 to 1997 and was the World Bank’s chief economist (1997 to 2000). Deep Dive Stiglitz said Trump’s tariffs would not bring production back to the US. He added that Trump “just doesn’t understand what to do”, citing coffee taxation. “Taxing coffee does not bring coffee production. We [US] don’t have the weather for it,” said Stiglitz, who shared the 2001 Nobel Prize in economics. His remarks came on the same morning that external affairs minister S Jaishankar said at the summit that India and the US had sorted out the bulk of issues in their trade talks and reached the finishing line. In a column in July, Stiglitz wrote that when another country has the means and the willingness to fight back, Trump “always chickens out”.

Nobel laureate economist Joseph E Stiglitz on Saturday questioned what a trade deal with the US was worth under President Donald Trump. He said Canada’s agreement with Washington had done little good. Stiglitz cited the EU example and said the US was pressing its trading partners to give up their sovereignty.

“Canada had a trade agreement with the US. What good did it do?” Stiglitz said at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in conversation with Dr Niranjan Rajadhyaksha, executive director of Artha Global.

He pointed to Europe’s attempt to control its digital economy and the worrying US response. “And the US said no, not if you are trading with us. And then you are giving up your sovereignty. That is something to be worried about,” said Stiglitz, who chaired Bill Clinton’s Council of Economic Advisers from 1995 to 1997 and was the World Bank’s chief economist (1997 to 2000).

Stiglitz said Trump’s tariffs would not bring production back to the US. He added that Trump “just doesn’t understand what to do”, citing coffee taxation. “Taxing coffee does not bring coffee production. We [US] don’t have the weather for it,” said Stiglitz, who shared the 2001 Nobel Prize in economics.

His remarks came on the same morning that external affairs minister S Jaishankar said at the summit that India and the US had sorted out the bulk of issues in their trade talks and reached the finishing line.
In a column in July, Stiglitz wrote that when another country has the means and the willingness to fight back, Trump “always chickens out”.

news.headline: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
news.story_lead: The lower stage of the rocket was diverted to the ocean as it burst into flames - Published 13 November 2026 SpaceX aborted its attempt to catch the bottom part of its huge Starship rocket during its latest test flight. The aim was to catch it using the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on the launch tower as it returned to Earth, but instead it was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames as it came down. The top part of the rocket is now continuing its journey to space, and SpaceX will decide whether it will try to catch this rocket stage at about 15:15 local time (21:15 GMT) on Saturday.
news.full_article_text: The lower stage of the rocket was diverted to the ocean as it burst into flames - Published 13 November 2026 SpaceX aborted its attempt to catch the bottom part of its huge Starship rocket during its latest test flight. The aim was to catch it using the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on the launch tower as it returned to Earth, but instead it was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames as it came down. The top part of the rocket is now continuing its journey to space, and SpaceX will decide whether it will try to catch this rocket stage at about 15:15 local time (21:15 GMT) on Saturday. It is the company's first attempt to fully recover its rocket, paving the way for making Starship fully reusable so it can fly repeatedly and reduce costs. Starship is the tallest and most powerful rocket ever built The 124m-tall rocket successfully blasted off from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas at 16:45 local time (22:45 GMT) on Friday. It was supposed to catch the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - six and a half minutes later when it returned to the launch tower, but instead it was diverted to the ocean. During a stream of the launch, a SpaceX spokesperson said: "Safety is always the number one priority, and we're still testing out things that we haven't done before on these vehicles, and so we are prioritising making sure that we can perform each maneuver safely." The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, is continuing its journey to space, where it is deploying 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high-speed internet from space. The Ship is due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning to the launch tower 22.5 hours after taking off, where a second catch may be attempted. SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights. But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead, it has splashed down in the ocean. Before the flight, SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it is in space. If any problems are detected, there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean. A SpaceX lander could take astronauts down to the surface of the Moon Building a fully reusable rocket is a long-held ambition for SpaceX. In 2015, it became the first company to vertically land part of a rocket with its Falcon 9 booster. Falcon 9 rockets now fly more than 100 times a year, and the ability to reuse the bottom part of the rocket has dramatically cut the costs of launch. But landing an entire Starship rocket could take this to the next level, says Prof Malcolm Macdonald, president of Royal Aeronautical Society. "Full reusability has the potential to fundamentally change the economics of accessing space," he said. "One successful flight will not prove that model, but it could mark an important transition: from demonstrating that Starship can fly, to demonstrating how Starship could operate." - What is Nasa's Artemis III mission? And what comes next? Published 27 October - Watch: From launch to fiery splashdown, SpaceX's Starship completes orbit test Published 28 September After SpaceX went public earlier this year, its shareholders will be carefully monitoring this flight, as will the US Space Agency. The progress of Starship has direct implications for Nasa's attempt to land humans on the Moon in 2028 - a highly ambitious timeline. SpaceX has been given a Nasa contract to configure the Ship into a lander that will eventually take astronauts down to the lunar surface. But it is not the only company working with the US Space Agency. Blue Origin, owned by rival tech billionaire Jeff Bezos, also has a contract to use its New Glenn rocket and lander for the Moon touch down. Both companies will also play a key role in Artemis III, which is currently planned for summer 2027- another challenging schedule. This mission will see four astronauts in Nasa's Orion spacecraft attempt to dock with both SpaceX and Blue Origin's landers. Starship will need to make a lot of progress in the coming months to meet these commitments - the pace of the rocket's development has been far slower than SpaceX had intended. But Blue Origin also has much work to do. The company suffered a major setback earlier this year when its rocket exploded, totally destroying its launchpad in Florida. Blue Origin had said they would be back in action by the end of this year, but a return to flight has now been delayed to early in 2027. Nasa is under pressure to meet its timelines. news.headline: India's Border Capability Improved Significantly Despite Active Border Dynamics, Says EAM S. Jaishankar
news.story_lead: Speaking at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi, External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar stated that India's border with China has become 'more alive', but emphasized that Indian force sustainment and infrastructure capabilities along the frontier have significantly improved over the last decade. He also noted that while India and China had comparable economic scales in the 1980s, China rapidly industrialized while India missed that development phase.
news.full_article_text:
Addressing the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit (HTLS 2026) in New Delhi, External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar reflected on the evolving security and economic dynamics between India and China. He noted that the border with China has become 'more alive in a way,' but highlighted that India's capacity to deploy and sustain armed forces along the frontier has experienced substantial enhancement. According to Jaishankar, border infrastructure had suffered from systemic neglect until roughly ten years ago, after which a deliberate policy shift led to major operational improvements.

Contextualizing the operational environment, the External Affairs Minister alluded to the violent June 2020 Galwan Valley clash, which resulted in the deaths of 20 Indian soldiers and unconfirmed casualties on the Chinese side. The incident severely damaged bilateral diplomatic relations, bringing them to a historical low.

In addition to security matters, Jaishankar drew a direct comparison between the historical economic trajectories of the two nations. He highlighted that when Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi visited China in 1988, both economies were roughly equivalent in size. However, China undertook an aggressive push toward industrialization and modernization throughout the 1980s, whereas India failed to capitalize on industrial development during the same period, creating a long-term economic gap between the two neighbours.

news.headline: EAM S. Jaishankar Outlines Foreign Policy Blueprint Driven by Domestic Manufacturing and Frontier Technologies
news.story_lead: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar detailed a strategic framework for navigating a shifting global order during the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi. He emphasized that domestic economic initiatives like Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India serve as the core building blocks of India's foreign policy. To maintain strategic autonomy, India must bridge historical manufacturing gaps while accelerating investments in emerging technologies like AI and semiconductors.
news.full_article_text:
### Foreign Policy Built on Domestic Economic Capacity

Speaking at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi, themed "New Rules. New Realities.", External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar stated that domestic flagship economic programs—including Atmanirbhar Bharat, Make in India, and Innovate in India—are fundamental building blocks of Indian foreign policy rather than standalone economic initiatives. In an interactive session with R. Sukumar, Editor-in-Chief of Hindustan Times, the minister highlighted that an effective external strategy in the contemporary era relies directly on robust national capabilities.

### Overcoming Historical Manufacturing Shortfalls

Jaishankar noted that while India has created a strong foundation over the past decade, the country historically "missed the manufacturing bus" during the period spanning the 1960s to the 1990s, describing those years as lost decades. He added that the economic reforms of 1991–92 acted only as a partial correction. To overcome these historical deficits, the government is utilizing targeted policy instruments such as the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme to reinvigorate neglected industries, support small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and enhance physical infrastructure alongside logistics networks.

### Strategic Investments in Frontier Technologies

To ensure long-term competitiveness in an evolving geopolitical landscape, the minister outlined the necessity of expanding domestic capabilities across frontier sectors. Key priorities include scaling up research and manufacturing in semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), and bio-life sciences. Additionally, strengthening educational institutions and expanding vocational skilling are critical to preparing the workforce for an AI-driven global economy.

### Navigating a Transactional Global Order

Addressing geopolitical trends, Jaishankar observed that traditional international alliances are becoming less cohesive and increasingly transactional. As global dynamics shift toward self-centred competition among nation-states, building internal strength across technology, manufacturing, and supply chain logistics becomes essential to maintaining strategic autonomy and effective global engagement.

नई दिल्ली में "न्यू रूल्स. न्यू रियलिटीज." थीम के तहत आयोजित 24वें हिंदुस्तान टाइम्स लीडरशिप समिट में बोलते हुए, विदेश मंत्री एस. जयशंकर ने कहा कि आत्मनिर्भर भारत, मेक इन इंडिया और इनोवेट इन इंडिया जैसे प्रमुख आर्थिक कार्यक्रम विदेश नीति के बुनियादी निर्माण खंड हैं। उन्होंने स्पष्ट किया कि इस दौर में एक प्रभावी विदेश नीति मजबूत राष्ट्रीय क्षमताओं के बिना संभव नहीं है।

### ऐतिहासिक विनिर्माण घाटे को पूरा करना

जयशंकर ने उल्लेख किया कि भारत ने पिछले दशक में एक मजबूत नींव रखी है, लेकिन देश 1960 के दशक से 1990 के दशक के दौरान विनिर्माण क्षेत्र में पिछड़ गया था, जिसे उन्होंने 'खोए हुए दशक' करार दिया। उन्होंने कहा कि 1991-92 के आर्थिक सुधार केवल आंशिक सुधार थे। इस अंतर को समाप्त करने के लिए सरकार प्रोडक्शन-लिंक्ड इंसेंटिव (PLI) जैसी योजनाओं का उपयोग कर रही है ताकि उपेक्षित उद्योगों और छोटे तथा मध्यम उद्यमों (SMEs) को बढ़ावा दिया जा सके।

### उभरती प्रौद्योगिकियों में रणनीतिक निवेश

बदलते भू-राजनीतिक परिदृश्य में प्रतिस्पर्धात्मक बने रहने के लिए, मंत्री ने सेमीकंडक्टर, आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस (AI) और बायो-लाइफ साइंसेज जैसे उभरते क्षेत्रों में घरेलू क्षमताओं को बढ़ाने की आवश्यकता पर बल दिया। इसके अतिरिक्त, AI-संचालित अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए कार्यबल को तैयार करने हेतु शैक्षणिक संस्थानों और व्यावसायिक कौशल का विस्तार करना आवश्यक है।

### लेन-देन पर आधारित वैश्विक व्यवस्था में नेविगेशन

वैश्विक भू-राजनीति के संदर्भ में, जयशंकर ने कहा कि पारंपरिक गठबंधन कम एकजुट और अधिक लेन-देन पर आधारित हो रहे हैं। जैसे-जैसे वैश्विक स्थितियां राष्ट्रों के बीच आक्रामक प्रतिस्पर्धा की ओर बढ़ रही हैं, रणनीतिक स्वायत्तता बनाए रखने के लिए प्रौद्योगिकी और विनिर्माण में आंतरिक क्षमताएं मजबूत करना अनिवार्य हो गया है।

news.full_article_text:
### Tributes Paid to India's First Prime Minister
On November 14, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh commemorated the 137th birth anniversary of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru. PM Modi extended his tributes through an official statement on X, recognizing Nehru's lasting contributions to the nation. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh highlighted Nehru's crucial involvement in India's freedom struggle and his leadership during the crucial founding years of independent India.

### Origins and Significance of National Children's Day
Across India, November 14 is celebrated annually as National Children's Day, locally known as 'Bal Diwas'. Jawaharlal Nehru, affectionately referred to as 'Chacha Nehru', was renowned for his deep fondness for children and his emphasis on child welfare and education. Born on November 14, 1889, in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, Nehru took office as the first Prime Minister of independent India on August 15, 1947, serving until his passing on May 27, 1964.

Following his death in May 1964, the Parliament of India unanimously adopted a resolution designating his birth anniversary as National Children's Day. Prior to this shift, India had observed Children's Day on November 20, coinciding with the Universal Children's Day established by the United Nations in 1954. Educational institutions nationwide celebrate the occasion with student competitions, sports, and cultural programmes, while political leaders and institutional heads, including President Droupadi Murmu, host commemorative events.
news.background_context: Initially, India celebrated Children's Day on November 20 following the United Nations declaration of Universal Children's Day in 1954. Following the death of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on May 27, 1964, the Indian Parliament passed a unanimous resolution to shift National Children's Day to November 14 to honor his life and love for children.

news.full_article_text: Chris Van Hollen (L) says he will challenge Chuck Schumer (R) and that the Democrats need new leadership - Published 13 November 2026, 15:48 GMT Senator Chuck Schumer is facing a challenge to his position as US Senate majority leader from his fellow Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen, as the party prepares to take control of Congress after sweeping the midterm elections. Van Hollen, 67, said in a post on X on Thursday that Americans voted for change earlier this month and "to deliver, we need new leadership". Schumer, 75, has led Democrats in the chamber since 2017, serving as both majority and minority leader. He was first elected to the Senate in 1999. Following the midterms earlier this month, his position has come under pressure by some left-wing Democrats who see him as too moderate and part of the party establishment. Responding to the challenge, Schumer, who represents New York, said he welcomed "any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead". He added that he was "proud of what we've accomplished together" in the midterms, and he had "the votes to continue as Democratic leader". The vote on Senate leader will be held behind closed doors in early December and the winner will assume the role on 4 January, when Democrats take control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives after their midterms successes. The move by Van Hollen, who represents Maryland, marks the most significant step by a high-profile Democrat to challenge the party's existing leadership following last week's midterms victory. Announcing his plans to run in a post on X, he wrote that Americans had called on the party to "unrig an economy rigged against working people". "We should not be preserving our institutions if they are not delivering for the American people," he said at a summit in Colorado hosted by majority Democrats. "And we should be making delivering for the American people the single mission of our government, even when that means shaking things up." He added: "This country does not belong to the people who can afford to buy influence. It belongs to all of us. And it's time we govern like that." In recent years, Van Hollen has taken positions popular with those on the left of his party. In 2024, he supported restricting weapons shipments to Israel and criticised the Biden administration over its role in the war in Gaza. In an interview with MS NOW, Van Hollen - who has served in the Senate for nearly a decade - acknowledged that he was an "underdog" but added that he believed the race was "very much in flux". Independent Senator Bernie Sanders and Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed have both publicly come out in support of Van Hollen - while others have also called for new leadership. In a post on X, Sanders said he believed Van Hollen "will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families". El-Sayed said the challenger would bring "bold leadership" and lead with both "courage and experience". Others Democrats have publicly backed Schumer. Senator Jacky Rosen of Nevada said: "He has the experience and the fight to continue leading our diverse caucus at this crucial moment". Senator Kirsten Gillibrand said: "You will see, despite all the grumblings, enormous gratitude for the hard work he has done to get us to this position." news.headline: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
news.story_lead: The Pope, who has Peruvian citizenship, lived in Chiclayo for several years - Published 1 hour ago Pope Leo XIV has celebrated mass near the Peruvian city where he made his name as a compassionate bishop who worked closely with poor and migrant communities. The ceremony was held on Friday at a park in Pimentel, about 10km (six miles) from Chiclayo in northern Peru as part of his tour of Latin America. The Vatican estimates more than 1.5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff.
news.full_article_text: The Pope, who has Peruvian citizenship, lived in Chiclayo for several years - Published 1 hour ago Pope Leo XIV has celebrated mass near the Peruvian city where he made his name as a compassionate bishop who worked closely with poor and migrant communities. The ceremony was held on Friday at a park in Pimentel, about 10km (six miles) from Chiclayo in northern Peru as part of his tour of Latin America. The Vatican estimates more than 1.5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff. "Thank you for your affection, support and prayers," the Pope told followers. "Especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God's help, I am overcoming," he added, referencing the surgery he had for lung cancer which took place just weeks ago . Some of the crowd arrived 12 hours in advance to wait in vigil before the mass began. "We spent the night praying, alongside family, excited to welcome the Pope from Chiclayo," said Isa Orderique. Pope Leo celebrated mass in front of a jubilant crowd Many came from across Peru and even neighbouring countries to attend. Merli Cruz Guerrero, from an area near the Ecuadorean border, travelled several hours by bus to attend. She also spent the entire night waiting. Of all the events the Pope has attended so far during his visit to Peru, this felt particularly emotional. The crowd fell into a hushed silence as the pontiff's motorcade approached. They waited eagerly for his arrival despite spending long hours out in the open with the temperature pushing past 30C. For many living here, the fact that the Pope worked extensively in this region before becoming the head of the Catholic Church has put them in the spotlight. "The Pope has come home and Chiclayo is celebrating," said Lisbeth DÃ­az, a teacher who worked with Pope Leo when he served as the city's bishop between 2015 and 2023. Lisbet DÃ­az says Chiclayo is celebrating the Pope's return Peru is the longest stop on the first tour of Latin America by the pontiff , who was elected in May 2025. The trip has also taken in Argentina and Uruguay, but his time in this country carries particular significance. The Pope not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities. Around Chiclayo, it is hard to meet anyone who doesn't claim to be a friend of the Pope or have a special anecdote about him. Some recall how he would enjoy sampling Peruvian delicacies at El TrÃ©bol, a restaurant next to the city's cathedral. Others remember his love of tennis. But for many it's the more serious moments of his time here, such as helping launch soup kitchens during the Covid-19 pandemic, or wading through deep waters on horseback when floods hit the area. Several of these images are on display in a small museum dedicated to him at the entrance to the bishop's residence. Commemorative pictures of the Pope are sold in the main of square of Chiclayo, including a famous image of him visiting a remote village on horseback But for the city, and for a country that calls him the "Peruvian Pope", his return home means much more than a collection of photographs and anecdotes. "It is the return of the man who brought Peruvians closer to the Church," said Samuel David Miranda Atoche, a local parish priest from Chiclayo who was ordained by the Pope back when he was still the bishop and known under his birth name of Robert Prevost. And it is not just local people he connected with, according to DÃ­az, who came to Chiclayo from Venezuela. "It was difficult for him to see so many migrants living on the streets," she added, recalling the time when large numbers of Venezuelans came through Chiclayo escaping the political and economic crisis in their home country. "So, he got in touch with the migration authorities and coordinated with other organisations to speed up the paperwork needed for many of us to obtain legal residency and work permits." - Who is Robert Prevost, the new Pope Leo XIV? Published 9 May 2025 Robert Prevost's time here as bishop also involved difficult decisions, such as having to deal with the controversy and scandal surrounding the dissolution of Sodalitium of Christian Life, a Peruvian Catholic organisation that had faced decades of sexual abuse allegations. Santiago Roncagliolo, a Peruvian writer and journalist who has studied the Pope's life, believes his handling of that crisis earned him the favour of his predecessor, Pope Francis, and helped set him on the path to the papacy. Father David also stressed the role the now-pontiff played in bringing people together. "If there is one thing Bishop Prevost worked for here," he added, referring to the Pope by his previous title, "it was unity". That unity has been on display in the run up to the mass, with the square in front of Chiclayo Cathedral filled with joyous celebrations for days. Father David says the Pope brought Peruvians closer to the Church Normally, 800,000 people live in the city and its surrounding area, but estimates say the Pope's visit has caused that to double. Local businesses have been capitalising on the Pope's popularity to boost sales and hotels have sharply increased their nightly room rates. But that didn't seem to put off the faithful who gathered for the mass. Shouts of: "The Pope is from Chiclayo!" echoed across the field during the event. Their affection was clearly reflected by the pontiff. "As I look at your faces, a prayer of thanksgiving to the Lord arises in my heart," he said from the stage, "for the blessing you have been and continue to be in my life." news.headline: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
news.story_lead: Watch: What we know so far about the Microsoft outage - Published 13 November 2026, 07:12 GMT A major Microsoft outage has impacted schools, healthcare systems, businesses, courts and governments around the world. Services including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot, are being restored almost 24 hours since issues first surfaced. Microsoft said the outage was not a cyber-security incident and was caused by a technical issue.
news.full_article_text: Watch: What we know so far about the Microsoft outage - Published 13 November 2026, 07:12 GMT A major Microsoft outage has impacted schools, healthcare systems, businesses, courts and governments around the world. Services including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot, are being restored almost 24 hours since issues first surfaced. Microsoft said the outage was not a cyber-security incident and was caused by a technical issue. It has apologised for the disruption. Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong. - Schools, GPs and businesses hit by global Microsoft outage as company scrambles to solve issue What happened? Some Microsoft 365 services have been affected by "connectivity problems" with problems reported in at least 74 countries. From late on Thursday, customers reported varying levels of access - many were unable to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps. But some users were able to use Teams, messaging and online meeting functions without issues. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe and improvement in North America. The company added that it was focused on "addressing the remaining areas of disruption" but warned "some users may still experience intermittent issues". In a later statement, the company said it was continuing to see improvements "with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels". The company attributed the ongoing outage to an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade. "We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions," it said on Friday. Will emails affected by the outage ever arrive? Although services are beginning to resume, Microsoft has warned of continued "intermittent access issues", meaning some users will still struggle to load their inboxes and could experience "delayed email delivery". In other words, it is not quite safe to assume every email you send is going to arrive in its intended recipient's inbox right away. Earlier, Microsoft said it would be extending the "timeout window" to 48 hours "to help protect delayed messages as delivery catches up". The email timeout window refers to the amount of time Outlook will wait to receive an email. When they do show up, the timestamp will be when they were delivered rather than when they were sent. Why has it taken so long to fix? Although email service Outlook appears to be resuming, the outage has so far lasted for more than 20 hours - in outage terms that is considered a long time. Prof James Ferryman from the University of Reading's department of computer science said the details the company has disclosed provide some clues. "What Microsoft has told us is that the part of its servers that sets up secure connections is getting swamped, and once that happens the server just stops answering," he said. It is, therefore, important that appropriate institutional initiatives are undertaken to familiarise students with the significance of Veer Baal Diwas and the sacrifices it commemorates, it says. ### Overview of the Controversy
Public friction within US President Donald Trump's cabinet has intensified following security concerns surrounding Nvidia's export of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductors. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's department for failing to promptly place cloud computing firm Megaspeed on the official trade entity control list despite warnings from multiple government agencies.

### Leadership Ouster and Espionage Allegations
The fallout was triggered by the ouster of Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang following revelations of an unapproved relationship with a businesswoman associated with Megaspeed. US intelligence agencies suspect the executive of ties to Chinese espionage operations aimed at bypassing trade restrictions to acquire critical AI infrastructure.

### Key Export Rules and Regulatory Failures
- **Export Policy Mandate:** President Donald Trump issued explicit directives prohibiting China from acquiring any Nvidia AI processors exceeding the performance capabilities of the H100 microchip.
- **Route and Tariff Loophole:** Under current policy mechanisms, Nvidia's higher-capacity H200 chips manufactured in Taiwan were permitted for export after being imported into the US for physical inspection and subjected to a 25% tariff under national security trade statutes.
- **Entity List Delays:** Although multiple federal intelligence and financial security agencies advocated placing Megaspeed on the US Entity List for months, administrative delays within the Department of Commerce prevented formal blacklisting.

### Congressional Inquiries and Legal Actions
1. **Senate Banking Committee Hearing:** Committee Chairman Tim Scott (Republican) summoned both Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to testify regarding security lapses in December 2026.
2. **Records Retention Demands:** Democrats on key congressional panels, led by House Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E. Neal and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden, demanded full retention of all administrative records and internal communications regarding Nvidia sales approvals.
3. **Investigation into Trade Enforcement:** Lawmakers highlighted that national security trade provisions intended to protect domestic technology were improperly utilized, allowing sensitive H200 processors to reach foreign end-users.

hindi_translation.story_lead: अमेरिकी वित्त मंत्री स्कॉट बेसेंट ने वाणिज्य मंत्री हावर्ड लुटनिक के विभाग पर चीन को उन्नत एनवीडिया आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस चिप्स के निर्यात को रोकने में ढिलाई का सार्वजनिक रूप से आरोप लगाया है। यह विवाद एनवीडिया के सीईओ जेन्सेन हुआंग को मेघास्पीड से जुड़ी एक महिला कार्यकारी के साथ संबंधों के उजागर होने के बाद पद से हटाए जाने के बाद सामने आया है।

### विवाद का अवलोकन
अमेरिका के राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्प के मंत्रिमंडल के भीतर एनवीडिया के उन्नत आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस (AI) सेमीकंडक्टरों के निर्यात को लेकर राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा चिंताओं के कारण आंतरिक मतभेद सार्वजनिक हो गए हैं। वित्त मंत्री स्कॉट बेसेंट ने कई एजेंसियों की सिफारिशों के बावजूद क्लाउड कंप्यूटिंग फर्म 'मेघास्पीड' को ब्लैकलिस्ट में डालने में देरी के लिए वाणिज्य मंत्री हावर्ड लुटनिक के विभाग को जिम्मेदार ठहराया।

### नेतृत्व में बदलाव और जासूसी के आरोप
यह विवाद एनवीडिया के मुख्य कार्यकारी अधिकारी (CEO) जेन्सेन हुआंग को पद से हटाए जाने के बाद शुरू हुआ। हुआंग का मेघास्पीड से जुड़ी एक महिला कार्यकारी के साथ अनधिकृत संबंध सामने आया था। अमेरिकी खुफिया एजेंसियों को संदेह है कि वह कार्यकारी चीनी जासूसी अभियानों से जुड़ी थी, जिसका उद्देश्य व्यापार प्रतिबंधों को दरकिनार कर एआई चिप्स हासिल करना था।

### प्रमुख निर्यात नियम और नियामक खामियां
- **निर्यात नीति निर्देश:** राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्प ने स्पष्ट निर्देश दिए थे कि चीन को H100 चिप्स से अधिक क्षमता वाले एनवीडिया एआई प्रोसेसर नहीं मिलने चाहिए।
- **मार्ग और टैरिफ की खामी:** मौजूदा व्यवस्था के तहत, ताइवान में निर्मित एनवीडिया की अधिक उन्नत H200 चिप्स को अमेरिका में निरीक्षण के लिए लाया जाता था और 25% शुल्क लगाकर निर्यात की अनुमति दी जाती थी।
- **एंटिटी लिस्ट में देरी:** यद्यपि कई सुरक्षा और वित्तीय एजेंसियों ने मेघास्पीड को एंटिटी लिस्ट में डालने का समर्थन किया था, लेकिन वाणिज्य विभाग की आंतरिक देरी के कारण आधिकारिक प्रतिबंध नहीं लगाया जा सका।

### संसदीय जांच और कानूनी कार्रवाई
1. **सीनेट बैंकिंग समिति की सुनवाई:** समिति के अध्यक्ष सीनेटर टिम स्कॉट ने वाणिज्य मंत्री हावर्ड लुटनिक और एनवीडिया के पूर्व सीईओ जेन्सेन हुआंग को दिसंबर 2026 में गवाही के लिए तलब किया है।
2. **रिकॉर्ड सुरक्षित रखने का आदेश:** कांग्रेस समितियों के वरिष्ठ नेताओं, जिनमें रिचर्ड ई. नील और रॉन वाइडेन शामिल हैं, ने एनवीडिया चिप्स बिक्री की मंजूरी से जुड़े सभी संचार और रिकॉर्ड सुरक्षित रखने के निर्देश दिए हैं।

hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### रणनीतिक अंतरिक्ष प्रौद्योगिकी के लिए वित्तीय समझौता

विज्ञान एवं प्रौद्योगिकी मंत्रालय के अंतर्गत विज्ञान एवं प्रौद्योगिकी विभाग (DST) के एक सांविधिक निकाय, प्रौद्योगिकी विकास बोर्ड (TDB) ने स्पेस-टेक स्टार्टअप एस्ट्रोम के साथ ₹64.05 करोड़ के समझौते पर हस्ताक्षर किए हैं। इस फंडिंग समझौते को भारत में उन्नत उपग्रह प्रणालियों के व्यावसायीकरण और तकनीकी विकास को समर्थन देने के लिए तैयार किया गया है।

### मुख्य फोकस: AI-ELINT उपग्रह

- **मूल प्रौद्योगिकी:** यह पहल आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस-संचालित इलेक्ट्रॉनिक इंटेलिजेंस (AI-ELINT) उपग्रह पेलोड विकसित करने पर केंद्रित है।
- **क्षमताएं:** ELINT प्रणालियां इलेक्ट्रॉनिक संकेतों और गैर-संचार प्रसारणों को इंटरसेप्ट, विश्लेषण और संसाधित करती हैं। पेलोड पर ही AI को एकीकृत करने से वास्तविक समय में स्वचालित डेटा प्रसंस्करण और खतरों की पहचान संभव हो जाती है।
- **सार्वजनिक-निजी सहयोग:** यह परियोजना एक सरकारी फंडिंग निकाय (TDB-DST) और एक निजी डीप-टेक स्पेस उद्यम (Astrome) के बीच एक संस्थागत साझेदारी का प्रतिनिधित्व करती है।

### रणनीतिक महत्व

स्वदेशी AI-ELINT अंतरिक्ष क्षमताओं को विकसित करने से राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा और अंतरिक्ष स्थितिजन्य जागरूकता मजबूत होती है। उपग्रह स्तर पर ही इलेक्ट्रॉनिक इंटेलिजेंस को संसाधित करने से निर्णय लेने के चक्र में भारी कमी आती है।
